Member journey

Every stage, every handoff, every owner.

Follow the journey from first contact to repeat relationship. Each stage shows its touchpoints, the accountable role, and the automations that support it.

  1. 01Discover, inquire and try2 automations
  2. 02Join, pay and onboard2 automations
  3. 03Book, attend and visit3 automations
  4. 04Train, track and engage4 automations
  5. 05Renew, rebook or pause2 automations
  6. 06Review, refer and return1 automation
01

Discover, inquire and try

People find a gym, salon, studio or coach on Google Maps, Instagram, aggregator apps or through a friend, then message on WhatsApp or Instagram. A fast, honest reply and an easy first class, visit or discovery call decide where they go.

Touchpoints

  • Google Business Profile and Maps
  • Instagram reels, comments and DMs
  • Click-to-WhatsApp ads and Meta lead forms
  • Fitness aggregator listings
  • Trial classes and discovery calls
  • Walk-ins and friend referrals

Accountable owner

Membership sales or front-desk lead

Automations on this stage

Discover, inquire and try · 2–3 weeks

Coaching inquiry and discovery call funnel

Turn Instagram comments and DMs, ad leads and WhatsApp messages into booked discovery calls with a short pre-call form, so coaches speak to prepared prospects and nobody waits days for a reply.

View the blueprint ↗Discover, inquire and try · 3–5 weeks

Trial class booking and membership conversion

Book trial classes and intro offers straight from ads, Google and WhatsApp, prepare the trainer or teacher, and follow up after the visit with published plans and a payment link, so every trial visitor gets a consistent path to membership.

View the blueprint ↗
02

Join, pay and onboard

The person commits: a membership, class pack, coaching program or retreat place. Deposits, installments and mandates are set up, and goals, health declarations and dietary needs are shared through secure forms with clear consent.

Touchpoints

  • Membership, package and program sale
  • Payment links, UPI Autopay and installments
  • Intake and health declaration forms
  • Retreat and teacher training applications
  • Welcome and onboarding messages

Accountable owner

Studio manager, program manager or lead dietitian

Automations on this stage

Join, pay and onboard · 4–6 weeks

Coaching intake and qualified plan workflow

Collect consented intake details through a secure form, route them to a qualified dietitian or nutritionist, and let AI handle the formatting work around the plan the professional writes, such as shopping lists and recipe swaps.

View the blueprint ↗Join, pay and onboard · 3–5 weeks

Retreat, workshop and teacher training enrollment

Run applications, deposits, installments, health declarations, room allocation and pre-arrival information for retreats, workshops and teacher trainings from one record, with the lead teacher deciding every application that needs judgment.

View the blueprint ↗
03

Book, attend and visit

Day-to-day bookings: classes, appointments, PT sessions and treatments. Capacity, waitlists, staff schedules, reminders and no-show rules meet here, and so do the billed records that drive staff commission.

Touchpoints

  • Class and appointment bookings
  • Waitlists and late cancellations
  • Reminders and patch test prompts
  • Check-in at the entrance or reception
  • Stylist, therapist and trainer schedules

Accountable owner

Front-desk or operations manager

Automations on this stage

Book, attend and visit · 3–4 weeks

Class booking, waitlists and automatic promotion

Let members book classes on WhatsApp or the app, hold fair waitlists, offer the next person a spot when one opens, and apply the late cancellation policy the same way every time.

View the blueprint ↗Book, attend and visit · 3–5 weeks

Salon booking, reminders and no-show handling

Book the right service with the right stylist or therapist for the right length of time, send reminders and patch test prompts, fill late gaps from a waitlist, and handle no-shows with one clear policy.

View the blueprint ↗Book, attend and visit · 2–4 weeks

Stylist and therapist commission and incentive statements

Calculate commissions and incentives on services, packages and retail from the salon's own billing records, show each stylist or therapist a running statement, and give the owner a reviewed payout sheet at month end.

View the blueprint ↗
04

Train, track and engage

Between visits, attention keeps people coming. Trainers notice attendance drops, PT balances stay visible, coaches review weekly check-ins, and salon clients get their stylist's own aftercare notes.

Touchpoints

  • Attendance patterns and trainer check-ins
  • PT session balances
  • Weekly coaching check-ins
  • Aftercare notes and product suggestions
  • Progress logs and photos shared with consent

Accountable owner

Head trainer, head coach or salon manager

Automations on this stage

Train, track and engage · 3–5 weeks

Attendance-drop alerts and trainer check-ins

Spot members and students whose visits fall below their own usual pattern, brief their trainer or teacher with context and a drafted personal message, and track whether anyone followed up, well before the renewal date.

View the blueprint ↗Train, track and engage · 2–4 weeks

Personal training package and session tracking

Track every PT package from sale to last session: sessions booked, completed and remaining, expiry reminders, trainer session logs and a monthly trainer statement that matches each member's balance.

View the blueprint ↗Train, track and engage · 3–5 weeks

Weekly coaching check-ins and progress logs

Send a structured weekly check-in, keep measurements, adherence notes and optional photos in one place, summarize each week for the coach, and send concerns to a qualified professional before anything else happens.

View the blueprint ↗Train, track and engage · 2–3 weeks

Aftercare notes and consented product suggestions

Send each client the stylist's or therapist's own aftercare notes and the products they actually recommended at the visit, with consent, and track retail follow-through without generic promotional blasts.

View the blueprint ↗
05

Renew, rebook or pause

Plans end, packages run out and services fall due. Clear notice, fair freeze rules, easy cancellation, timely rebooking reminders and polite payment recovery protect revenue and trust at the same time.

Touchpoints

  • Renewal and auto-renewal notices
  • Freeze and cancellation requests
  • Failed payment recovery
  • Rebooking reminders by service interval
  • Win-back for lapsed members

Accountable owner

Membership or client experience manager

Automations on this stage

Renew, rebook or pause · 3–5 weeks

Renewals, freezes and payment recovery

Tell members clearly before a plan ends or auto-renews, offer renew, change, freeze or cancel options under the written policy, recover failed payments politely, and keep one record of every decision.

View the blueprint ↗Renew, rebook or pause · 2–3 weeks

Service-based rebooking reminders

Remind each client when their next service is due, based on the service they had and the interval their stylist recommends, with a one-tap link to book the same stylist.

View the blueprint ↗
06

Review, refer and return

Satisfied members and clients bring friends and leave reviews. Every client is asked the same way, problems reach a manager before they reach a review site, and referral rewards follow published terms.

Touchpoints

  • Private feedback forms
  • Google reviews and replies
  • Referral links and rewards
  • Milestone messages

Accountable owner

Owner or marketing lead

Automations on this stage

Review, refer and return · 2–4 weeks

Feedback, review invitations and referral program

Ask every client for private feedback after a visit or milestone, invite everyone to review the same way, route problems to a manager, and run a referral program whose rewards are never tied to reviews.

View the blueprint ↗

Where people stay in control

Human checkpoints across the journey.

Automation handles the predictable steps. These are the decisions that stay with an accountable person.

AutomationStageHuman checkpoint
Coaching inquiry and discovery call funnelDiscover, inquire and tryThe coach or dietitian runs every discovery call and decides whether the program suits the person. Anyone who mentions a medical condition is routed to a qualified professional. Automated replies never promise results, diagnose or suggest diets.
Trial class booking and membership conversionDiscover, inquire and tryThe trainer reviews readiness answers before the session and decides whether medical clearance is needed. The membership consultant owns the conversation, pricing and any discount within the limits the owner sets. Automation never diagnoses or tells anyone they are fit to exercise.
Coaching intake and qualified plan workflowJoin, pay and onboardA qualified dietitian or nutritionist writes and signs off every plan and every change to it. Clients who report a condition on the referral list see their doctor or a clinical dietitian first. AI never sets calorie targets, recommends supplements or gives medical advice.
Retreat, workshop and teacher training enrollmentJoin, pay and onboardThe lead teacher decides every application with health flags or eligibility questions. The program manager approves exceptions to payment schedules, transfers and refunds. Health declarations are read by people and never scored automatically.
Class booking, waitlists and automatic promotionBook, attend and visitThe studio manager sets capacity, cutoffs and the late cancellation policy, and personally decides any fee, credit deduction or booking restriction for repeat no-shows. Instructors decide how to adapt a class for anyone flagged.
Salon booking, reminders and no-show handlingBook, attend and visitThe salon manager approves every deposit retention, fee and booking restriction. Stylists check patch test results in person and decide whether a service goes ahead. Anyone reporting a reaction is told to stop and seek medical advice, and the manager is alerted.
Stylist and therapist commission and incentive statementsBook, attend and visitThe owner or HR lead approves the commission plan, every manual adjustment and the final payout sheet. The manager resolves queries against the original bill. The automation calculates; it never changes pay rules or pays anyone on its own.
Attendance-drop alerts and trainer check-insTrain, track and engageTrainers or teachers decide whether and how to reach out, and edit every drafted message before it is sent. Any offer or discount needs the manager's approval. Health-related replies go to a person and are never answered by automation.
Personal training package and session trackingTrain, track and engageTrainers confirm sessions and own the renewal conversation. The manager approves extensions, transfers, refunds and any dispute over session counts. Trainers write and adjust exercise programs; the automation only tracks and reminds.
Weekly coaching check-ins and progress logsTrain, track and engageCoaches review every summary and send every reply themselves. Plan changes are made only by the qualified dietitian or nutritionist. Concern flags reach a qualified professional the same day, and clients with possible medical issues are advised to see their doctor.
Aftercare notes and consented product suggestionsTrain, track and engageStylists and therapists choose every recommendation themselves; AI only tidies the wording of their notes. Any client reporting irritation, a burn or a reaction is called by the manager and advised to seek medical advice.
Renewals, freezes and payment recoveryRenew, rebook or pauseThe manager approves freezes outside policy, refunds, transfers, pro-rata adjustments and any discount. Front-desk staff call members with repeated payment failures. Automation never blocks access or ends a plan without a person's decision, except to carry out a member's own cancellation.
Service-based rebooking remindersRenew, rebook or pauseStylists set or change the interval for each client. The salon manager approves the default intervals and the reminder wording. Any offer or discount in a reminder needs manager approval.
Feedback, review invitations and referral programReview, refer and returnThe manager handles every low score personally and approves every public reply, refund or goodwill gesture. Referral rewards beyond the published terms need owner approval. Staff are never given review quotas.
